lawyer:
Aminul Islam, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Ariful Islam, Advocate -----For the Respondent No.2.
parties:
Rokaiya Amin ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi has been issued on 5-11-2012 at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to receive entire decretal amount with interest, if any, from the petitioner by 12 equal installments of one month each starting from January, 2013 and/or such other or further order or orders passed as this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Subsequently, this Court has issued another Supplementary Rule on 12-5-2014 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the proceedings of Artha Jari Case No. 142/2009 arising out of the Judgment and Decree dated 25-2-2009 passed by the Respondent No.3 in Artha Rin Suit No. 145/2007 so far as relates to sale or disposal otherwise of the mortgaged property situated out- side the territorial jurisdiction of the Executing Court should not be declared void, illegal and without jurisdiction and as to why the Order No. 12 dated 23-6-2010 allowing an application of the Decree Holder Bank filed under provision of section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuance of a Certificate of Title connected to the mortgaged property and Order No. 24 dated 26-5-2011 sending the said Certificate for registration passed by the Respondent No.3 in Artha Jari Case No. 142/2009 (Annexure-'E') should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect, and/or such other or further order or orders passed as this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Facts relevant for the disposal of this Rule in brief, are that the Respondent No. 2 Jamuna Bank Ltd. as Plaintiff' filed Artha Rin Suit No. 145 of 2007 in the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka against the petitioner and Others as defendants for recovery of Taka 27,37,944 contending inter alia that at the request of one Mr. Shahabuddin Talukder, the defendant No.1 in Suit, the Plaintiff Bank granted a Cash Credit facility of Taka 20, 00,000 to him who enjoyed the same upon renewal from time to time. The defendant No.1 having failed to pay the said outstanding dues to the Bank as per terms and conditions of the sanction letter, the Bank filed the Suit for recovery of the same. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement. The Artha Rin Adalat after hearing decreed the suit against the Defendant No. 1 on contest and ex parte against the rest on 25-2- 2009. In the suit the petitioner has been made defendant No. 3 as being 3rd party mortgagor.

4. The Decree-Holder Bank put the decree in execution by filing Artha Execution Case No. 142 of 2009. In the Execution Case the mortgaged property was placed on auction under Section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Ain") but no bidder participated in the auction. Thereafter, the Adalat directed the Decree Holder Bank to take step under section 33 (4) of the Ain fixing 22-4-2010 and then 23-6-2010 for holding auction. The Bank though took step under section 33 (4) of the Ain for holding auction of the mortgaged property for the second time but did not publish notice in the dailies, as directed by the Adalat. Subsequently, the Bank instead of taking step for publication of the auction notice in the dailies filed an application under section 33(7) of the Ain on 23-6-2010 praying for issuance of a certificate vesting the title of the mortgaged property in the Decree Holder Bank. The Adalat allowed the application and issued a certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain as prayed for and sent the same to the concerned Sub-Registration office for registration. After obtaining certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain, the petitioner came to know that the Bank is trying to sell the property at a shockingly low price to any person. Thereafter, the petitioner hurriedly rushed to the Bank and placed a positive proposal on 22-10- 2012 agreeing to pay the decretal amount with a view to save her property from auction and requested the Bank to allow her installments to pay the amount within 6(Six) months, but the Bank refused the proposal of the petitioner. At this stage the petitioner moved this Court by filing this Writ Petition for a direction upon the Bank to receive decretal amount with interest and to redeem the mortgage and obtained the present Rule and Stay.

5. Subsequently, the petitioner obtained a Supplementary Rule on 12-5-2014 on the ground of territorial jurisdiction of the Executing Court as the property in question is situated in the District Rajbari.

6. The Respondent No.2 Bank contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in opposition and Counter Affidavit denying the material facts made in the petition contending, inter alia, that the petitioner filed an application before the Executing Court on 13-1-2010 praying two months time to pay the decretal amount by four instalments. The Court allowed the prayer by its order dated 10-2-2010, but the petitioner did not pay any of the instalments. However, after registration of the certificate in favour of the Bank the petitioner filed the instant Writ Petition only to obstruct disposal of the property and to delay the recovery of the Bank's dues and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. It is also stated that the petitioner never approached the Bank with any proposal to pay the decretal amount before filing of the instant writ petition. During pendency of this Rule the petitioner by two identical applications dated 10-2-2013 and 2-7-2013 respectively approached the Bank. In reply to the said letters the Bank on 16-7-2013 sent a letter with registered A/D wherein the Bank invited the petitioner to sit with them to resolve the dispute amicably fixing 27-7-2013 at 10.00 A.M. However, said letter was returned unserved as the recipient was not found at the address. In such a situation the Bank sent two of its officials at the address wherein they were informed by the landlord of the building that the petitioner had moved away from the address five years back. Further case of the Respondent No. 2 is that the title of the property in question has already been vested in the Bank by a certificate issued by the executing Court on 26-5-2011 under section 33(7) of the Ain before issuance of this Rule and partial possession of the land has already been delivered to the Bank. Since the title of the property in question vested in the Decree Holder Bank long before the filing of this petition, at this belated stage there is no scope for the petitioner to get her property back.

7. Mr. Aminul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner firstly, submits that admittedly the mortgaged property is situated in District Rajbari. Given that the decree in the Artha Rin Suit was passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Dhaka, it has no jurisdiction to deal with the property situated beyond its territorial jurisdiction either by auction or by issuing a certificate of title. It is indeed the duty of the Executing Court as well as the Decree Holder to send/transfer the Execution Case to the Court having territorial jurisdiction to deal with the property in execution proceedings under section 27(1) of the Ain read with sections. 38 and 39 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code"). And as such issuance of a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain by the Executing Court having no territorial jurisdiction over the property is illegal and without lawful authority. Secondly, Mr. Islam submits that the Decree Holder having taken steps under Section 33(4) of the Ain for auction of the mortgaged property for the second time it cannot apply for granting certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain jumping over the provisions as contained in Section 33(5) & (6) of the Ain and as such, issuance of the certificate of title in favour of the Decree Holder without taking recourse to section 33(5) and (6) of the A in is palpably illegal and without lawful authority. It is also argued that the Decree Holder can ask for a certificate of title of the property only after taking recourse to section 33(1) of the Ain without taking any step under section 33(4) as provided in Section 33(7) of the Ain. But in the present case the Decree Holder in total violation of the provision of section 33(7) obtained the certificate of title of the mortgaged property and as such the certificate of title is not sustainable in law and liable to be declared to have been issued by the Court without lawful authority and in violation of law. Thirdly, Mr. Aminul Islam, submits, that, intention of the legislature is to recover the money from the loanee, but not to acquire the property of the mortgagor, borrower or guarantor by the bank. Therefore, whenever the Judgment-debtor approaches a bank to pay the decretal amount, it is incumbent upon the Decree Holder to receive the money and to redeem the mortgage in favour, of the mortgagor. He also submits that redemption of mortgage is a legal right of the mortgagor. Mere acquisition of title by a certificate issued by the Court under section 33(7) of the Ain does not ipso facto dis-entitle the mortgagor to have the mortgage redeemed upon payment of the decretal amount to the Bank. Since it is a legal right, the, right of redemption subsists. until a third party's interest gets involved in the property. In the present case no third party interest is involved and as such the Bank is under an obligation to release the property in favour of the petitioner upon receipt of the decretal amount. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Smt. Uma Kanoria vs Pradip Kumar Daga reported in AIR 2003 Cal 162, Shaba Yeshwant Naik vsVinod Kumar Gosalin reported in AIR 1985 Bombay 79, Hari Das Basu vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. reported in AIR 1932 Calcutta 213, Prem Chand Dey vs Mokhoda Debi reported in 17 ILR (1990) 699 and a judgment of this Court passed in World Resources Ltd. Vs Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka reported in 66 DLR 637, and section 27(1) of the Ain along with Sections 38 and 39 of the Code.

8. Mr Ariful Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No.2 Decree Holder Bank firstly submits that the provisions of Section 27(1) of the Ain and sections 38 and 39 of the Code are applicable in the case of Money Decree only and not in a case of Mortgage Decree. Because, in a Mortgage Decree the property in question is not required to be attached before auction sale as the property being a part of the decree is under the custody and control of the Court which passed the decree and can be put into execution for auction sale. But in a Money Decree if any property is required to be attached which is situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the court, the court is under an obligation to transfer the Decree to a competent court having territorial jurisdiction over the property as it cannot attach the property outside its territorial jurisdiction. Therefore, since the decree in question is a Mortgage Decree the executing court is not required to transfer the decree to the court where the property is situated and as such in the instant case the certificate issued by the Dhaka Court, vesting title of the property in the Decree Holder Bank is valid and lawful and cannot be questioned. Moreover, putting emphasis on the word "may" occurring in section 39(1) of the Code he submits, that it is the discretion of the Executing Court to decide whether it will send the case to another court for execution.

9. Secondly, Mr Ariful Islam states that the Suit was decreed in 2009, the certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain vesting the title of the mortgaged property in the Decree Holder Bank was issued on 26-5-2011, and pursuant to the said certificate partial possession of the property has already been delivered to the Decree Holder. Bank. In this situation the Petitioner-Judgment-debtor raised the question that the property was not within the jurisdiction of the Court at Dhaka for the first time. This objection to jurisdiction was not raised until the execution proceedings ended with the issuance of Certificate and therefore, it comes too late. Mr Islam submits that the petitioner cannot raise questions as to jurisdiction at a belated stage of the proceedings when the execution case has already been disposed of. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catenae of cases namely, Jagernath Sahai vs Dip Rani Koer reported in 22 ILR (1895) 871, Messrs, HN Dutta and Co. vs Smt. Tarubala Dassireported in AIR 1937 Cal 570, Tarach and vs. Misrimal reported in AIR 1970 Rajasthan, 58, Laxmi Narain vs Firm Ram Kumar Suraj Box reported in AIR 1971 Rajasthan 30, Sakil Nath Roy Chowdhury Vs Jessore United Bank Ltd. reported in AIR 1939 Calcutta 403, Begg, Dunlop and. Co. vs Jagannath Marwari reported in 16 CWN 402, Maseyk vs Steel and Co. and another reported in 14 ILR (1887) 662, Gopi Mohan Roy vs Doybaki Nundun Sen reported in 19 ILR (1891) 13 and Shaikh Abdul Hadi. vsMst. Kabultunnissa reported in 80 IC (1924) 901.

10. Heard the learned Advocates for the par- ties, perused the Application, Supplementary Affidavits, Affidavit-in-Opposition, Counter Affidavit and the Annexures annexed thereto.

11. In the instant Rule the first question raised is whether the Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka can issue a certificate declaring the title of the property vested in the Decree Holder under Section 33(7) of the Ain where the property is situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the said Court. To meet the question raised, Section 27(1) of the Ain along with Sections 38 and 39 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be looked into which run thus:-

২৭। (১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশ বা ডিক্রি উক্ত আদালত কর্তৃক, অথবা উক্ত আদালত জারীরজন্য অন্য যে আদালতে প্রেরণ করে, সেই আদালত কর্তৃক জারী হইবে।

Sections 38 and 39 CPC:

S 38. Court by which decrees may be executed-A decree may be executed either by the Court which passed it or by the court to which it is sent for execution.

S 39. Transfer of decree-The Court which passed a decree may, on the application of the decree-holder, send it for execution to another Court,-

(a) if the person against whom the decree is passed actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or

(b) if such person has no property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed the decree sufficient to satisfy such decree and has property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or

(c) if the decree directs the sale or delivery of immovable property situated outside the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed it, or

12. It appears from the language as used in the above quoted section 27(1) that should the mortgaged property be situated beyond the jurisdiction of the Executing Court, it is incumbent upon the court to send the case to the court having local jurisdiction for execution of the same. In the present case, admittedly, the property is situated in Rajbari District, but the Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka initiated the process of auction and issued the certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain which is absolutely beyond its territorial jurisdiction as per provisions contained in section 27(1) of the Ain and sections 38 and 39 of the Code.

13. It is evident from section 27(1) of the Ain, that this section provides for an execution case to be instituted in the court which passed the decree, and that for the convenience of execution, that court may send the execution case to another court and the said power is vested with the Adalat in which the case is filed and the Adalat may on its own motion send the execution case or upon an application filed by any of the parties or the Decree Holder requesting to exercise its power.

14. The above provisions of the Ain are basically similar to that of Sections 38 and 39 of the Code which provides the provisions for institution and transfer of an Execution Case.

15. Now the question is whether the Artha Rin Adalat is under a legal obligation to transfer the Execution Case to another Adalat of the District where the property in question situates. To answer the question the provisions in Section 33(1) of the Ain may be looked into which runs thus:

৩৩(১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত ডিক্রি বা আদেশ জারীর সময় কোন সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় ক্ষেত্রে বাদীর খরচে বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচারের তারিখ হইতে অন্যূন ১৫(পনের) দিবসের সময় দিয়া সীলমোহরকৃত টেন্ডার আহবান করিবে, উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তিকমপক্ষে বহুল প্রচারিত একটি বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, তদুপরি ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজন মনে করিলে স্থানীয় একটি  পত্রিকায়, যদি থাকে, প্রকাশ করিবে; এবং আদালতের নোটিশ বোর্ডে লটকইয়া ও স্থানীয়ভাবে ঢোল সহরত যোগও উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচার করিবে।

16. This section as quoted, above provides provisions for fixing of the auction notice in the notice board of the Executing Court and beating of drum in the locality. The action of beating of drum in the locality invariably requires to take place where the property is situated or in its immediate vicinity. The purpose of beating the drum in the locality is that the people of that locality must be made aware that the property in question is in the process of auction sale.

17. In view of such requirement of Section 3.3(1) of the Ain, it is not possible for the Adalat in Dhaka to send its process server or "Dhuli" to the territorial jurisdiction of another Adalat of a different district. The reason is simple, namely, the order of the Executing Court cannot be executed beyond its territorial limit for publicity by the Dhuli, without the assistance of the process server or "Dhuli" of another Court in whose jurisdiction the order is to be carried out. Moreover, without compliance of such requirement the auction sale cannot be legally held.

18. It is not disputed, that when a decree is passed by the competent Artha Rin Adalat the execution case has to be filed in that Court under section 27 of the Ain, but if the decree has to be satisfied by way of auction or otherwise the Execution Case needs to be transferred to the court where the property is situated. However, the word "may" occurring in section 39(1) of the Code or in section 27(1) of the Ain might give an impression about the discretion of the court where the Execution Case is filed. Almost in all the cases referred to by the learned counsels of both the parties the intent and purport of the word "may" has been exhaustively discussed unanimously in the Apex Courts of Indian Jurisdiction came to a common finding that the provisions of section 39 plainly indicate the acceptance by the legislature of the general principle that no court can execute a decree in which the subject matter of the suit or of the application for execution property is situated entirely outside the local limits of its jurisdiction.

19. In the unreported case of S. Co. Cement Limited represented by its Managing Director vs Artha Rin Ada/at No.4, Dhaka (Writ Petition No. 5360 of 2010) a Division Bench of this Court held that:

"The mortgaged property in relation to an auction sale situated in another District the Artha Rin Adalat is under a legal obligation to send the execution case to the concerned Artha Rin Adalat of the other District where the property is situated. This is unavoidably necessary for proper execution and satisfaction of the decree" (Per Md. Emdadul Huq, J).

20. Therefore, the certificate issued by the Court indeed, had no jurisdiction and as such the issuance of certificate by the Artha Rin Adalat in Dhaka is illegal and without jurisdiction.

21. The second question raised is whether the Artha Rin Adalat can issue a certificate on an application filed by the Decree Holder under section 33(7) of the Ain when it took steps under section 33(4) of the Ain for holding further auction of the mortgaged property and, thereby obviating the necessity of following the provisions contained under section 33(5) and (6) of the Ain. To meet the question as raised in the instant case the provisions of Section 33(5) and (7) of the Ain may be looked. into which runs thus:-

৩৩। (৫) কোন সম্পত্তি [উপ-ধারা] (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুয়ারে] বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রীকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধিতত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রিদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রিদার [উপ-ধারা] (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুয়ারে]

উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রির দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।

(৭) উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও, ডিক্রিদার উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তি মালিকানা সত্ত্বে পাইতে আগ্রহী মর্মে আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালত,উপ-ধারা  (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনরূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া। উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে; এবং ডিক্রিদারের পার্থিমতে  উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ব ডিক্রিদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা প্রদানপূর্বক তৎমর্মে একটি সনদপত্র জারী করিবে এবং জারীকৃত এইরুপ সনদপত্র স্বত্বের দলিল, হিসাব গণ্য হইবে; এবং আদালত উহার অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট  স্থানীয় সার-রেজিস্ট্রারের অফিসে নিবন্ধনের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবে।

22. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provisions of law it appears that in the event of having a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain the Decree Holder Bank is required to follow the provisions of section 33(1) to (3) and shall refrain from taking any steps under sub-sections (4) and (5). But in the present case the Decree Holder took steps under Section 33(4) for holding further auction of the mortgaged property. It is noted that for the purpose of getting a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain the law does not enjoin upon a Decree Holder Bank to take steps under section 33(4) of the Ain. However, as in the present case, when the Bank takes steps under section 33(4) there is no escape route to sidetrack or jump over the provisions of section 3(5) and (6). The Decree Holder Bank in this situation ought to have invoked the process under section 33(5) of the Ain upon the failure of the auction and thereafter to follow other' provisions as contained in Section 33(6) of the Ain. Evidently the Decree Holder Bank deviating from that sequential process instead of taking resort to the aforesaid provisions of law straightway applied under section 33(7) of the Ain praying for issuance of the certificate declaring title of the mortgaged property vested in the Bank. This Court finds such invocation of the law to be contrary to the provisions contained in Section 33(7) of the Ain. As per provisions of law once the Decree Holder takes step under Section 33(4) for holding further auction there remains no option but to follow the said provision to its statutorily intended and prescribed conclusion and progressing in stages through the express provisions of section 33(5) (6) and (7) of the Ain.

23. Since the Artha Rin Adalat issued a certificate directly under section 33(7) of the Ain without allowing prior necessary recourse to the provisions of section 33(5) and (6), the impugned order passed by the court is, accordingly, found to be illegal.

24. Apart from these, if we consider the Certificate of Title issued under section 33(7) to be a valid one, in that case, there is yet another aspect to the case before us, that is, whether the petitioner's right of redemption of the mortgage remains alive and extant as on the date of issuance of the Rule notwithstanding the issuance of Certificate of Title under section 33(7) of the A in when the petitioner before us, i.e. Mrs. Rokaiya Amin made overtures to meet the entire claim of the Bank. To meet this question the provision contained in section 5(4) of the Ain may be looked into which runs thus;

৫। (৪) The Transfer of Property Act, 1982 অথবা বর্তমান প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনে বিপরীত যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীনে বন্ধকী যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীন বন্ধকী মামলা ব্যাতিরেকে, এই আইনের অধীন দায়েরকৃত কোন মামলায়,আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রি বাদী প্রতিষ্ঠানের পক্ষে নিষ্ক্রিয় সমাপ্তির (Force clouser) প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে;এবং ঋণের বিপরীতে বাদীর অনুকূলে বন্ধকী স্থারব সম্পত্তি ডিক্রির ধারাবাহিকতায় নিলাম বিক্রয় মাত্রই উক্ত প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি চুড়ান্ত ও ক্রয় বৈধ গণ্য হইবে এবং অতঃপর উক্ত সম্পত্তি পুনরুদ্ধার করিবার কোন রুপ অধিকার (Right to redeem) বিবাদী দায়িকের থাকিবে না।

25. It is evident that under section 5(4) in the case of suit for sale on the basis of a mortgage, as is the case in the present instance, preliminary decree shall become final upon an auction sale taking place and concomitantly the right to redemption shall be deemed to come to an end at that point in time. It is clear from the law that until such auction sale and final decree, the right to redeem remains intact. Applied in conjunction with section 33(7), however, that deeming provision of section 5(4) may very well be argued to meet its limitation in the circumstances envisaged in section 33(7) given that the fact or concept of an. auction sale does not arise in section 33(7) scenario. In that scenario the very issuance of Certificate of Title and its registration thereof may be construed by many as a finality of the Execution process, thereby, extinguishing a right of redemption at the point of such issuance. The petitioner's respond to that line of thinking by stressing that the right to redeem is in fact a legal and substantive right to property which ought not to be extinguished by mere implication given that section 33(7) remains silent on the extinguishments of the capacity to redeem existing in any mortgagor. It is pointed out that this question of redemption could also have been better understood, should section 5(4) have borne express reference to the status of a right of redemption in the context of section 33(7), But clearly section 5(4) bears no such reference to section 33(7). It is, accordingly, argued that such absence of specific declaration of the law extinguishing the right of redemption on the issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title, it would be misconceived to expressly find on such extinguishments to the detriment of a mortgagor and this would go beyond the rules of either statutory interpretation or construction. This Court finds merit in these submissions as the petitioner is willing to redeem the mortgage upon satisfaction of the Bank's outstanding claims in its totality.

<u>26. This Court is of the view that the transfer of title under section 33(7) does not indeed envisage the right of foreclosure. In the scheme of the Act, foreclosure in the sense of a Imitation on the right of redemption can only arise when associated with an auction sale contemplated in section 5(4), Beyond that, section 33(7) appears to this Court to operate independently of section 5(4) and the provisions in section 33(7) in not contemplating a transfer, by sale must be found also not to envisage the existence, of the corresponding right of foreclosure. Therefore, the right of redemption under section 33(7) is always found to be alive and extant.</u>

<u>27. It is also relevant to note that section 33(9) of the Act speaks of a final disposal of an execution case on, inter alia, issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title. That provision, however, remains qualified by certain amendments introduced into the Act in 2010 adding Sections 33(7ক) and (7খ) facilitating delivery of possession to the property as coursed by the Certificate of Title. These latter provisions, as are to be read as independent and self-contained provisions in section 33, are declaratory of the legislative intent to revive an execution case on certain specified grounds, if need be, even after court's declaration of conclusion of an execution process under section 33(9).</u>

<u>28. Indeed, sections 33(7ক) and (7খ) have no bearing on the question of the right of redemption but these go to establish the fact that even upon a Section 33(7) Certificate of Title being issued the executing court does not necessarily become functus officio immediately thereafter. That view facilitates a better understanding, therefore, of the effect of declaring the Execution Case No. 142 of 2009 to be finally disposed of under Section 33(9) upon registration of the Certificate of Title granted. Indeed in the present instance the Court assumed jurisdiction under section 33(7ক) notwithstanding, it is this Court's view that the right of redemption of mortgage has never stood extinguished at any material time. Accordingly, it was always open to the petitioner in particular in the facts and circumstances to seek redemption of her mortgage upon a settlement arrived at with the bank or financial institution concerned, So, once the loan repayment is forthcoming, the Adalat will correspondingly find it within its power to permit such repayment and recovery of loan, thereby, doing that which is right and just as contemplated in section 57.</u>

29. This understanding of the law and considering the rights and responsibilities of the parties in the context of section 33(7) leads this Court to hold that the petitioner before us is still entitled to redeem the mortgage upon making payment of the bank's outstanding.

30. Taking into consideration, the above, this Court finds the Impugned Orders to be seriously wanting in legal sufficiency and contrary to the relevant provisions of flaws and principles and, thereby, to be shorn of all. validity and legal effect.

31. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. Accordingly this Court hereby declares the Impugned Orders dated 23-6-2010 and 26-5-2011 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat issuing Certificate of Title and thereby sending the same for registration respectively to be illegal and without lawful authority. The petitioner is directed to meet the outstanding claim of the Bank within a period of 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Judgment and Order.

32. The petitioner is put on notice that such liability shall have to be met in conformity with the Artha Rin Decree subject to the express provision of the law. Similarly, it shall be incumbent upon the Respondent No.2 Bank to facilitate and ensure the due redemption of the mortgage by the petitioner in accordance, with law upon receipt of full payment of all its outstanding claim. Any failure by the petitioner to comply with the directions above shall automatically entitle the respondent No.2 Bank to proceed and deal in and with the property in question in accordance with law after transferring the case to the Artha Rin Adalat Rajbari as per provision of section 27(1) of the Ain.

33. The ad interim Order of restraint as initially granted is, hereby, recalled and vacated.

There is no order as to costs.

Communicate this order at once.

End.
